title: The only backup that counts is the one you have restored

videos.script: Ask a team whether its database is backed up, and the answer is yes. {{question}} Ask what that yes rests on, and the answer is a job that runs every night. {{job}} A job that exits cleanly proves that a program ran. It does not prove that the data comes back. {{chain}} In this lesson you build the machine for the whole course. One Ubuntu computer, with PostgreSQL on it, that you are allowed to break. {{lab}} Then you copy a small shop, and restore the copy. {{restore}} You check the restore the only honest way, by asking both databases the same questions and comparing the answers. {{report}} Then you damage the copy on purpose, and watch the check find one missing order in fifty thousand. {{broken}} Last, you run a backup command that reports success and saves twenty bytes. {{pipe}} It is one of the commonest backup lines there is. By the end of the lesson you will know why it is not a backup.
